expert_term.en: expert appointed by the investigative body, prosecutor or court: a forensic expert of a state forensic institution, a registered private expert, or another person with specific expertise

appointment.basis: Kriminaalmenetluse seadustik (KrMS), section on ordering an expert assessment not verified
appointment.summary_en: In the pre-trial stage the investigative body (police) or the prosecutor appoints the expert; at trial the court. There is no obligation to appoint an expert from the official lists; on request, the Estonian Forensic Science Institute (EKEI) assigns a forensic expert.

questions.summary_en: The expert may refuse the assessment if the material provided is insufficient, if the tasks in the order fall outside the expert's expertise, or if answering does not require expert research or conclusions based on specialist knowledge (§ 98(1) p 4); a refusal is recorded in a refusal act stating the data of § 107(1) p 1-9 and the reasons (§ 108). Whether the expert may report facts not asked about was not verified.

report_contents.basis: KrMS § 107 (Ekspertiisiakti koostamine), as amended by RT I, 03.02.2023, 1 (in force 01.05.2023 per search extract)
items_en: identification and procedural data listed in § 107(1) points 1-8 (not verified individually)
measures applied to the physical evidence, comparison material or examination object submitted (point 9)
reasoning: description of the research, analyses, tests or other work needed to form the opinion (point 10)
in a commission, the dissenting expert's opinion attached; the report is confirmed by the expert or experts who performed the assessment

rights_duties.basis: KrMS § 98 (rights and duties of expert; detail not verified); Kohtuekspertiisiseadus
rights_duties.summary_en: Court-appointed experts have a statutory duty to disclose conflicts of interest; experts must notify all parties of the start of the assessment and must work thoroughly, completely and objectively with scientifically reasoned opinions (per Estonian contact-point information on e-Justice).

appointment.basis: Tsiviilkohtumenetluse seadustik (TsMS), expert-assessment provisions (section numbers not verified)
appointment.summary_en: At a participant's request the court may order an expert assessment for circumstances requiring specific expertise (and on its own motion for foreign or international law). The assessment is done by a forensic expert or other specialist of a state forensic institution, an officially certified expert, or another person with specific expertise appointed by the court; others only with good reason where a certified expert is available; an expert agreed by the parties is appointed if legally eligible. Instead, the court may use an expert opinion ordered in other court, criminal or misdemeanour proceedings.

questions.summary_en: Participants may pose questions to the expert through the court; the court determines which questions require an expert opinion and gives reasons for rejecting questions. At the hearing the court excludes questions that are irrelevant or outside the expert's competence. Reporting facts not asked about was not verified.

items_en: detailed description of the examinations carried out
conclusions reached as a result of the examinations
reasoned answers to the court's questions

rights_duties.summary_en: The expert must give a correct and reasoned opinion on the questions; may examine the case materials as needed, take part in examining evidence in court and request reference material and additional data from the court. The opinion is written unless the court orders otherwise; the expert may be summoned for questioning, and must be if a party requests. Witness-hearing rules apply to hearing experts.

statute.title_local: Kohtuekspertiisiseadus (KES), in force from 01.09.2023 (Riigi Teataja akt 103022023001)
statute.title_en: Forensic Examination Act; EKEI keeps the list of registered private experts (entry for three years, after taking the registered private expert's oath)

liability.summary_en: Giving a knowingly false expert opinion is a criminal offence under KarS § 321; maximum penalty not verified. Experts are also liable under general contract and tort law; no mandatory professional indemnity insurance.
